 Kymera Therapeutics Announces Proposed Public Offering 
 Watertown, Mass. (November 23, 2026) — Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: KYMR), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing a new class
of oral small molecule degrader medicines for immunological diseases, today announced that it has commenced an underwritten public offering of $1.5 billion of shares of its common stock. All of the shares of common stock to be sold in this
offering are being offered by Kymera. In addition, Kymera intends to grant the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional $225 million of shares of its common stock at the public
offering price per share, less underwriting discounts and commissions. The proposed offering is subject to market and other conditions, and there can be no assurance as to whether or when the offering may be completed, or as to the actual size or
terms of the offering. 
 Kymera intends to use the net proceeds from the offering to continue to advance its pipeline of preclinical and clinical degrader
programs that are designed to address large patient populations with significant need and clear commercial opportunity, and for working capital and other general corporate purposes. 
 Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, Jefferies, TD Cowen, Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Stifel and Wells Fargo Securities are acting as joint book-running
managers for the offering. 
 The securities described above are being offered pursuant to an automatically effective shelf registration statement on Form S-3 (No. 333-282912) that was filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on October 31, 2024. This offering is being made only by
means of a prospectus supplement and an accompanying prospectus that form a part of the registration statement.

 About Kymera Therapeutics 
 Kymera is a clinical-stage
biotechnology company pioneering the field of targeted protein degradation (TPD) to develop medicines that address critical health problems and have the potential to dramatically improve patients’ lives. Kymera is deploying TPD to address
disease targets and pathways inaccessible with conventional therapeutics. Having advanced the first degrader into the clinic for immunological diseases, Kymera is focused on building an industry-leading pipeline of oral small molecule degraders to
provide a new generation of convenient, highly effective therapies for patients with these conditions. Founded in 2016, Kymera has been recognized as one of Boston’s top workplaces for the past several years.

 Kymera Therapeutics Announces Positive Results from BROADEN2 Phase 2b Clinical Trial of KT-621, a First-in-Class, Oral STAT6 Degrader, in Patients with Moderate to Severe Atopic Dermatitis 
 BROADEN2 met primary and secondary endpoints with statistically significant improvements versus placebo at Week 16 across all doses,
reinforcing KT-621’s transformative potential 
 KT-621 clinical efficacy profile was at least comparable to approved pathway biologics with
statistically significant EASI and itch improvements versus placebo as early as Week 1 
 KT-621 achieved 45% placebo-adjusted mean EASI reduction, 40% placebo-adjusted EASI-75, and 38% placebo-adjusted ≥ 4-point PPNRS response in the mid dose cohort 
 KT-621 was well-tolerated with a favorable safety profile 
 First KT-621 Phase 3 AD trial planned to start by mid-2027; 
BREADTH Phase 2b asthma trial ongoing, with topline data expected to be reported by late 2027 
 Company to hold video conference call
and webcast today at 8:00 a.m. ET 
 Watertown, Mass. (November 23, 2026) – Kymera Therapeutics, Inc . (NASDAQ: KYMR), a
clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing a new class of oral small molecule degrader medicines for immunological diseases, today announced positive 16-week results from the BROADEN2 Phase 2b trial of
 KT-621, its first-in-class, once-daily oral STAT6 degrader, in patients with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (AD). The trial
met its primary endpoint of percent change from baseline in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score at Week 16 and secondary endpoints, with statistically significant improvements versus placebo across all dose cohorts. The BROADEN2 findings
support advancement of KT-621 into late-stage development, with the first Phase 3 AD trial planned to initiate by mid-2027, subject to alignment with regulators, as well
as potential expansion in other Type 2 indications. 
 “Today’s results mark a pivotal moment in the field of immunology, demonstrating what
truly groundbreaking science can achieve in areas of significant patient need. The BROADEN2 results exceeded our expectations, reinforcing our belief that KT-621 represents one of the largest opportunities in
biopharma, with the potential to transform care for millions of people living with Type 2 inflammatory diseases,” said Nello Mainolfi, PhD, Founder, President and CEO, Kymera Therapeutics. “What stands out is the combination of
improvements in disease severity and itch beginning as early as Week 1, significant continued responses across all dose cohorts at Week 16, and a favorable safety profile. The overall clinical activity supports the potential to deliver the level of
disease control historically reported with approved biologics such as dupilumab. The mid dose, which we selected to achieve optimal STAT6 pharmacology, consistently delivered the largest numerical improvements across endpoints and is well positioned
to advance towards Phase 3.” 
 Dr. Mainolfi continued, “These findings strengthen our conviction that KT-621 could substantially expand the number of patients receiving an advanced therapy. By overcoming the longstanding scientific challenge of directly targeting STAT6, we have taken a clear step toward our vision
of delivering the first oral therapy for the full spectrum of Type 2 diseases, beginning in AD. Additionally, these results validate the scientific expertise and translational capabilities behind our innovation engine and our approach of pairing the
right targets with the right technology to create a new era of oral medicines. As we advance KT-621 toward Phase 3, we are building an expanding franchise with the potential to reshape care across immunology.
Importantly, we thank the patients and their families for their trust and commitment, and the investigators and study teams for their dedication to advancing this unique new treatment for AD.” 
 “In my practice, I see many patients living with AD who continue to struggle with persistent symptoms and the daily burden of managing this chronic
condition,” said Eric Simpson, MD, MCR, lead investigator on the BROADEN2 study and Frances J. Storrs Medical Dermatology Professor and Director of CLEAR Eczema Center, Oregon Health & Science University. “A targeted oral
therapy that combines robust clinical activity with favorable safety and tolerability could expand the number of patients receiving systemic treatment and help them achieve and maintain disease control. KT-621 
brings an innovative mechanism to a well-established pathway in Type 2 inflammation by targeting STAT6. The highly encouraging BROADEN2 findings suggest a compelling profile and reinforce the potential of this program to address the substantial
unmet need in AD.” 
 BROADEN2 Phase 2b Trial Design and Baseline Characteristics 
 BROADEN2 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, dose-ranging trial evaluating the clinical activity, safety and tolerability of KT-621 in 244 adult and adolescent patients with moderate to severe AD. Patients were randomized (1:1:1:1) to receive a low dose (n=61), mid dose (n=61) or high dose (n=63) of
 KT-621, or placebo (n=59), once daily for 16 weeks. Patients completing 16 weeks of treatment were eligible to participate in a 52-week open-label extension following
the treatment period. 
 Baseline characteristics were generally balanced across the four treatment groups. The mean baseline EASI score was approximately
28, and the mean baseline Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (PPNRS) score was 7.1. Patients with severe disease based on a validated Investigator Global Assessment for Atopic Dermatitis (vIGA-AD) score of 4
represented 38% of the study population, and 33% of patients had received prior biologic therapy. Of the 244 randomized patients, 234 completed the 16-week double-blind treatment period, and 230 of those
patients enrolled in the open-label extension. 
 BROADEN2 Phase 2b Results at Week 16 
 Exposure and degradation profiles of each dose were in line with what was reported in Phase 1 studies. All three KT-621 
doses met all the primary and secondary endpoints, with statistically significant improvements versus placebo at Week 16. The mid dose, which was selected to achieve the optimal STAT6 pharmacology, consistently delivered the largest numerical
improvements across all efficacy endpoints. 
 Primary endpoint: KT-621 demonstrated rapid onset of activity,
with statistically significant EASI improvement versus placebo as early as Week 1 with improvements continuing through Week 16. 
 | 
 • | Percent change from baseline in EASI: A 72% mean reduction was achieved by the mid dose patients versus
27% in the placebo arm at Week 16 representing a placebo-adjusted difference of 45% (p<0.0001). Mean reductions of 64% (p<0.0001) and 61% (p<0.0001) were achieved by the low dose and high dose patients, respectively. 
 | 
 Secondary endpoints on clinical responses and itch relief: At Week 16,
 KT-621 demonstrated statistically significant rapid and robust improvements in AD signs and symptoms at all doses, including substantial reductions in disease severity, clear or almost clear skin responses and
pronounced itch relief: 
 | 
 • | EASI-75 (at least a 75% improvement from baseline in EASI
score): EASI-75 was achieved by 62% of the mid dose patients versus 22% in the placebo arm (p<0.0001). | • | EASI-90 (at least a 90% improvement from baseline in EASI
score): EASI-90 was achieved by 43% of the mid dose patients versus 10% in the placebo arm (p<0.0001). | • | vIGA-AD 0/1 (clear or almost clear skin, with at least a
 2-point reduction from baseline ): vIGA-AD of 0 or 1 was achieved by 38% of the mid dose patients versus 11% in the placebo arm (p=0.0008). | • | PPNRS (mean percent change and
 ≥ 4-point improvement from baseline): A 58% mean reduction in PPNRS was achieved by the mid dose patients versus 21% in the placebo arm (p<0.0001). A ≥4-point PPNRS reduction was achieved by 52% of mid dose patients versus 13% in the placebo arm (p<0.0001). 
 | 
 Safety and tolerability 
 KT-621 was well-tolerated over 16 weeks, with a favorable safety profile. Most treatment-emergent adverse events were
mild or moderate with no dose response or meaningful imbalances in placebo versus treatment arm with the exception of conjunctivitis, as seen in other pathway agents. Pooled conjunctivitis rates (all terms) were 19.7% for the low dose, 13.1% for the
mid dose and 11.1% for the high dose. All conjunctivitis events in KT-621-treated patients were mild to moderate, and none led to treatment discontinuation. Across all
study arms, four participants reported serious adverse events (SAEs). Events included atopic dermatitis (2), hand fracture (1), and schizoaffective disorder (1, in a participant with a prior history of this condition). All were deemed unrelated to
study drug. 
 Next Steps 
 Based on the BROADEN2
results and subject to alignment with regulators, Kymera plans to advance KT-621 into Phase 3 development in AD, with the first trial expected to initiate by mid-2027. 
 The ongoing BREADTH Phase 2b trial is evaluating KT-621 in moderate to severe eosinophilic asthma, with topline
data expected in late 2027. These studies are intended to accelerate KT-621 development in, and enable dose selection for, subsequent parallel Phase 3 registrational studies across multiple Type 2 dermatology,
gastroenterology and respiratory indications.

 About KT-621 
 KT-621 is an investigational,
 first-in-class, once daily, oral degrader of STAT6, the specific transcription factor responsible for
 IL-4/IL-13 signaling and the central driver of Type 2 inflammation. KT-621 is currently in clinical development in atopic
dermatitis (AD) and asthma . In the BROADEN2 Phase 2b trial in AD, KT-621 met its primary and secondary endpoints, demonstrating statistically significant improvements, rapid onset of activity and sustained
responses through Week 16. KT-621 was well tolerated with a favorable safety and tolerability profile. KT-621 has the potential to become the first oral medicine for a
wide range of Type 2 inflammatory diseases, offering a safe, effective option that could bring advanced therapy to millions of underserved patients worldwide, including those living with AD, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD),
eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE), chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), prurigo nodularis (PN) and bullous pemphigoid (BP), among others. 
 About Atopic Dermatitis 
 Atopic dermatitis (AD) is the
most common form of eczema, a chronic inflammatory disease that causes the skin to become inflamed and irritated, making it extremely pruritic (itchy). AD occurs most frequently in children but also affects adults. It can affect a patient’s
quality of life and lead to additional complications, such as infections and sleep loss. While there are currently available medicines for AD, such as topical therapies and injectable biologics, there remains a significant unmet need and opportunity
to improve treatment options for millions of patients. Learn more about AD on Kymera’s website . 
 About Kymera Therapeutics 
 Kymera is a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the field of targeted protein degradation (TPD) to develop medicines that address critical health
problems and have the potential to dramatically improve patients’ lives. Kymera is deploying TPD to address disease targets and pathways inaccessible with conventional therapeutics. Having advanced the first degrader into the clinic for
immunological diseases, Kymera is focused on building an industry-leading pipeline of oral small molecule degraders to provide a new generation of convenient, highly effective therapies for patients with these conditions. Founded in 2016, Kymera has
been recognized as one of Boston’s top workplaces for the past several years. For more information about our science, pipeline and people, please visit www.kymeratx.com or follow us on X or LinkedIn .

 KT-621 BROADEN2 Phase 2b Trial 
 On November 23, 2026 we announced the results from our BROADEN2 Phase 2b trial of KT-621, the Company’s first-in-class, once-daily oral STAT6 degrader, in patients with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (AD). 
 BROADEN2 Phase 2b Trial Design and Baseline Characteristics 
 BROADEN2 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, dose-ranging trial evaluating the clinical activity, safety and tolerability of KT-621 in 244 adult and adolescent patients with moderate to severe AD. Patients were randomized (1:1:1:1) to receive a low-dose (n=61), mid-dose (n=61) or high-dose (n=63) of KT-621, or placebo (n=59), once daily for 16 weeks. Patients completing 16 weeks of treatment were eligible to participate in a 52-week open-label extension following the treatment period. 
 Baseline characteristics were generally balanced across the four treatment groups. The mean baseline EASI score was approximately 28, and the mean baseline Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (PPNRS) score was 7.1. Patients with severe disease based on a validated Investigator Global Assessment for Atopic Dermatitis (vIGA-AD) score of 4 represented 38% of the study population, and 33% of patients had received prior biologic therapy. Of the 244 randomized patients, 234 completed the 16-week double-blind treatment period, and 230 of those patients enrolled in the open-label extension. 
 BROADEN2 Phase 2b Results at Week 16 
 Exposure and degradation profiles of each dose were in line with what was reported in Phase 1 studies. All three KT-621 doses met all the primary and secondary endpoints, with statistically significant improvements versus placebo at Week 16. The mid dose, which was selected to achieve the optimal STAT6 pharmacology, consistently delivered the largest numerical improvements across all efficacy endpoints. 
 Primary endpoint: KT-621 demonstrated rapid onset of activity, with statistically significant EASI improvement versus placebo as early as Week 1 with improvements continuing through Week 16. 
 | 
 • | Percent change from baseline in EASI : A 72% mean reduction was achieved by the mid dose patients versus 27% in the placebo arm at Week 16 representing a placebo-adjusted difference of 45% (p<0.0001). Mean reductions of 64% (p<0.0001) and 61% (p<0.0001) were achieved by the low dose and high dose patients, respectively. 
 | 
 Secondary endpoints on clinical responses and itch relief : At Week 16, KT-621 demonstrated statistically significant rapid and robust improvements in AD signs and symptoms at all doses, including substantial reductions in disease severity, clear or almost clear skin responses and pronounced itch relief: 
 | 
 • | EASI-75 (at least a 75% improvement from baseline in EASI score): EASI-75 was achieved by 62% of the mid dose patients versus 22% in the placebo arm (p<0.0001). | • | EASI-90 (at least a 90% improvement from baseline in EASI score): EASI-90 was achieved by 43% of the mid dose patients versus 10% in the placebo arm (p<0.0001). | • | vIGA-AD 0/1 (clear or almost clear skin, with at least a 2-point reduction from baseline ): vIGA-AD of 0 or 1 was achieved by 38% of the mid dose patients versus 11% in the placebo arm (p=0.0008). | • | PPNRS (mean percent change and ≥ 4-point improvement from baseline) : A 58% mean reduction in PPNRS was achieved by the mid dose patients versus 21% in the placebo arm (p<0.0001). A ≥4-point PPNRS reduction was achieved by 52% of mid dose patients versus 13% in the placebo arm (p<0.0001). 
 | 
 Safety and tolerability 
 KT-621 was well-tolerated over 16 weeks, with a favorable safety profile. Most treatment-emergent adverse events were mild or moderate with no dose response or meaningful imbalances in placebo versus treatment arm with the exception of conjunctivitis, as seen in other pathway agents. Pooled conjunctivitis rates (all terms) were 19.7% for the low dose, 13.1% for the mid dose and 11.1% for the high dose.
